title: Finite-component form of the ring-theoretic dimension maximum
statement: Under the hypotheses of the minimal component dimension maximum theorem, there is a finite nonempty set of exactly the minimal primes below p, all quotient dimensions are at most d+r, and one attains d+r.

proof.text: Use Noetherianity to form the finite nonempty set of minimal primes below p, then use localization prime correspondence and maximal prime-chain lengths to bound every quotient dimension by d+r and attain the bound by concatenating a chain below p with a maximal chain above p.

minimal primes finite nonempty localization prime correspondence chain length

lean.statement: theorem minimal_component_dimension_maximum_data {k : Type u} [Field k] {S : Type v} [CommRing S] [Algebra k S] [Algebra.FiniteType k S] (p : Ideal S) [p.IsPrime] (d r : ℕ) (hd : ringKrullDim (Localization.AtPrime p) = (d : WithBot ℕ∞)) (hr : Algebra.trdeg k p.ResidueField = (r : Cardinal.{v})) : ∃ qs : Finset (Ideal S), (∀ q : Ideal S, q ∈ qs ↔ q.IsPrime ∧ q ≤ p ∧ (∀ t : Ideal S, t.IsPrime → t ≤ q → t = q)) ∧ qs.Nonempty ∧ ((∀ q ∈ qs, ringKrullDim (S ⧸ q) ≤ ((d + r : ℕ) : WithBot ℕ∞)) ∧ (∃ q ∈ qs, ringKrullDim (S ⧸ q) = ((d + r : ℕ) : WithBot ℕ∞)))
